newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philippine officials meet exiled rebels.
newsitem.headline: Philippine officials meet exiled rebels.

text.p: Philippine government representatives met exiled Communist rebels in a luxury Amsterdam hotel on Monday in a bid to breathe new life into their country's faltering peace process.

"We hope to bring the NDF (National Democratic Front) into the process," a government spokesman said ahead of talks between Jose de Venecia, speaker of the Philippine House of Representatives, and Jose-Maria Sison, NDF chief political consultant.

Peace talks between the two sides being conducted in the Dutch city of Utrecht, where Sison lives in exile, have run into difficulties over the government panel's refusal to acknowledge human rights violations, Sison said in a statement ahead of today's meeting.

"The (government) negotiating panel...deny the perpetration of human rights violations even under the Marcos regime," the statement said. As a result the government-NDF negotiations had run into "serious difficulties".

The NDF further charges the government with obstructing claims by victims of human rights abuses to Swiss-held assets on accounts opened by former Philippine dictator Ferdinand Marcos who ruled the country for 14 years until he was overthrown in a 1986 popular revolt.
